extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and practitioners handling inter partes reexamination proceedings at the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP governing what submissions are permitted, how defective or late papers are handled, petition requirements to revive reexamination prosecutions, examiner timing and action choices (ACP/NIRC/non-ACP), and related clerical/cover-sheet/signature requirements for inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on party iterations of input
rubrics_metrics.description: After an opposition to any patent owner petition is filed by a third party requester (regardless of entry rights), any further paper in opposition/rebuttal/response to the third party opposition paper will not be considered and will be returned; likewise, after an opposition to any requester petition is filed by the patent owner, any further paper in opposition/rebuttal/response to the patent owner opposition paper will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be a limitation on party iterations of input, especially given the statutory mandate for special dispatch in reexamination. Petitions requesting denial of an extension of time by a requester will be returned since a requester has no statutory right to challenge discretionary procedural processes of the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit on behalf of third parties (other than third party requester)
rubrics_metrics.description: No submissions on behalf of any third parties other than third party requesters as defined in 35 U.S.C. 100(e) will be considered unless in accordance with 37 CFR 1.915 or are exceptions noted in the MPEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper submitted by a third party other than a third party requester must be (1) a 37 CFR 1.501 art citation limited to the citation of patents and printed publications and an explanation of pertinency and applicability, or (2) bare notice of suits and other proceedings involving the patent (including copies of decisions or court papers). Such submissions must be without additional comment and cannot include further arguments or information. Other submissions will be returned or destroyed. If a permitted submission contains additional material beyond scope, it will be returned or destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers (patent owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by the patent owner which are unsigned, or signed by less than all of the patent owners where no attorney or agent is of record or acting in representative capacity, will be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned patent owner papers will be retained in the file but denied consideration. See 37 CFR 1.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proof of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by the patent owner (or third party requester where proof is required) that lack proof of service may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers should be denied consideration where it cannot be determined that service was in fact made and another party’s response/comment/appeal/brief period is to be set by the date of service. See 37 CFR 1.248 and MPEP § 2666.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late papers (patent owner and third party requester)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed after the period for response set by the Office will be retained in the file but will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critical date is the date of service (not the Office receipt date). Examples: a patent owner submission filed after the permitted time from the date of service of a third party requester’s submission will be retained but not considered. Similarly, third party requester submissions filed after the permitted time from the date of service of the patent owner’s submission will be retained but not considered. For oppositions to petitions where a right exists, oppositions must be filed within two weeks of service to ensure consideration; oppositions after two weeks remain of record but are not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment to the description and claims which does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k) will be retained in the file but will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: where the only defect in the amendment is that it enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent or introduces new matter, such an amendment will be considered and a rejection will be made in the next Office action. New matter amendments to the disclosure will be required to be canceled and claims containing new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. New matter to drawings is ordinarily not entered. An amendment that enlarges the scope of the claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a). See MPEP §§ 2234, 2250, 608.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of appeal or notice of cross appeal is filed before a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) has been issued, the paper will be retained in the file but will not be considered (other than to inform the parties that the appeal is not acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.61 and procedures for handling premature notices of appeal in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of defective papers by third party requester (unsigned/no proof/late/premature appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by a third party requester which are unsigned, lack proof of service where required, are untimely, or are premature appeals will be denied consideration or retained but not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned: denied consideration (37 CFR 1.33). No proof of service: may be denied (37 CFR 1.248). Late third party comments following a patent owner response (e.g., 37 CFR 1.947 submissions) are retained but not considered; date of service on third party requester is critical. Premature appeals: retained but not considered (37 CFR 41.61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage area for late art citations
rubrics_metrics.description: A storage area for submissions of art citations in an inter partes reexamination will be maintained separate from reexamination and patent files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art citations based solely on prior patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are retained in the storage area and are not entered into the patent file but delayed until reexamination proceedings conclude. Proper timely art citation submissions made prior to the order are placed in the reexamination file. See 37 CFR 1.501 and 1.902; CRU handles storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival petition — unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive a terminated reexamination prosecution based on unavoidable delay must provide an adequate showing that the entire delay was unavoidable and include supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed), the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(l), details of the circumstances surrounding the unavoidable delay and evidence to support the showing, and a proposed response to continue prosecution (unless previously filed). These provisions import 35 U.S.C. 133 into reexamination via 35 U.S.C. 305 and 314.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival petition — unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive a terminated reexamination prosecution based on unintentional delay must include a verified statement that the entire delay was unintentional and related filing items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition must be accompanied by the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed), the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m), a verified statement that the entire delay was unintentional, and a proposed response to continue prosecution (unless previously filed). The fee provisions of 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewed petition for reconsideration of denied revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration of a decision refusing to revive a prosecution must be requested within one month of the decision’s mail date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time for renewed petitions are only available under 37 CFR 1.956; 1.136 extensions are not available in reexamination. A renewed petition should include a cover letter entitled “Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a)” for unavoidable or “Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b)” for unintentional petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: All petitions to accept late papers and revive decided in OPLA
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions in reexamination proceedings to accept late papers and revive will be decided in the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical handling by CRU support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: CRU support staff will carry out clerical handling and processing of inter partes reexamination cases, performing PALM matters and making copies and transmittals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks include PALMing the file to the examiner, copying decisions/Office actions for patent owner and third party requester(s), making copies of needed references, completing transmittal form PTOL-2070 with requester’s address, coordinating with examiner and CRU SPEs/TC QASs and paralegals. Amendments complying with 37 CFR 1.941 are entered by CRU clerical staff. See MPEP §§ 2234, 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments (effect and new matter handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is submitted in proper form and otherwise appropriate, the amendment will be entered for purposes of the reexamination proceeding though the amendment does not have legal effect until the certificate is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any “new matter” amendment to the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132) will be required to be canceled and claims containing new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. A “new matter” amendment to the drawing is ordinarily not entered. Where an amendment enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent, the claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a). For merged proceedings see MPEP §§ 2686.01 and 2686.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after patent owner response and third party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: After response by the patent owner and any third party comments, the patent under reexamination will be reconsidered and parties will be notified of claims rejected, claims found patentable, and any objections or requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner may respond to such Office action with or without amendment, and the third party requester may provide comments after the patent owner’s response. If the patent owner’s response contains an amendment, the examiner will consider whether the amendment raises issues of 35 U.S.C. 112 and/or broadening of claims under 35 U.S.C. 314. Reconsideration continues until ready for closing prosecution, at which point the examiner will issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for examiner pre-action consultation and Office action issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner receives the case file (patent owner response and any requester comments), the examiner will prepare for a pre-action consultation conference with a Reexamination Legal Adviser (RLA); the consultation should be completed within two weeks and the Office action prepared no later than two weeks from the date of the consultation conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise authorized by the CRU Director or an OPLA RLA. After preparation, the case is forwarded to the CRU SPE/TC QAS for review; any returns for correction/revision must be handled expeditiously and returned within the time set by the SPE/QAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for Office action to issue (ACP, NIRC, non-ACP) depending on parties’ responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner has discrete options depending on whether the patent owner responded and whether third party comments were timely: issue NIRC if no patent owner response and all claims are rejected; issue ACP if at least one claim is patentable; issue incomplete-response action, Notice of Defective Paper, ACP, or a new non-closing Office action depending on completeness/formality/readiness; handle third party comments that exceed permitted scope under MPEP § 2666.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: (A) No timely patent owner response: (1) if all claims rejected issue NIRC; (2) if at least one claim free of rejection issue ACP (with statements on limitation of proceeding). Examiner may still issue supplemental OA if new info warrants a new rejection. (B) Timely patent owner response but no timely requester comments: options include incomplete-response action (MPEP § 2666.30), Notice of Defective Paper (MPEP § 2666.50), ACP if ready, or a new office action not closing prosecution (MPEP § 2671.01). (C) Timely response and timely comments: similar handling plus procedures for improper or out-of-scope comments (MPEP § 2666.05). (D) Expedited RAN issuance possible under 37 CFR 1.953(b) if criteria satisfied; see MPEP § 2673.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for issuing an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACP is issued when the patent owner’s response is complete and defect-free and the proceeding is ready for closing prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding is ready for closing prosecution if all claims are determined to be patentable, all claims are determined to be rejected, or some claims are determined patentable and some rejected. After an ACP, requirements of 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced and amendments after an ACP require a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they were not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and comprehensiveness required for non-ACP Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-ACP Office action should be comprehensive and similar in form to a first Office action but addressing the patent owner’s response and third party comments; it should state the examiner’s position so that the next action can properly be an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should address all issues related to the patents or printed publications, clearly set forth each ground of rejection/objection and the reasons supporting them, and clearly set forth each rejection proposed by the third party requester that the examiner refuses to adopt with reasons. Comprehensive reasons for patentability must be given for favorable determinations. See MPEP § 1302.14 for examples of suitable statements of reasons for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of amendatory matter under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment has been submitted in the patent owner’s response, the amendatory matter (revised or newly added matter) should be reviewed for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review based upon 35 U.S.C. 112 of the content of the patent that has not been revised is not proper in reexamination and should not be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when examiner withdraws a rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection originally initiated by the examiner, such withdrawal should be clearly stated as a decision favorable to patentability with respect to the withdrawn rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection previously proposed by the third party requester (e.g., based on patent owner’s argument or evidence), the examiner should treat the issue as a rejection proposed by the third party requester that the examiner refuses to adopt. If claims have been amended and the examiner withdraws a ground previously proposed by the third party requester as to the original claims, generally this is not a refusal to adopt the requester’s rejection (since it was never proposed as to amended claims), but the requester may re-propose the rejection as to amended claims. If the patent owner fails to respond to actions leading to a RAN and a RAN is issued, the third party requester may appeal such withdrawals as final decisions favorable to patentability (see 37 CFR 41.61(a)(2)). Special handling applies where a dependent claim is amended in certain ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not within scope of reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If issues not within the scope of reexamination proceedings (e.g., questions of patentability based on public use or on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) have been raised by the patent owner or third party requester, the examiner will note the existence of such questions in the Office action using form paragraph 26.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.03 states the issue is not within scope of inter partes reexamination and will not be considered, and advises the patentee that filing a reissue application may be desirable. If such issues were independently discovered by the examiner (but not raised by owner or requester), they should not be noted because 37 CFR 1.906(c) is directed only to issues raised by the patent owner or third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action cover sheet (PTOL-2064) and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTOL-2064 should be used as the Office action cover sheet; since the Office action is responsive to communications, the date(s) of the communication(s) should be filled in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, the patent owner is given two months to respond to the action; thus the PTOL-2064 space for the date of the communication(s) should reflect 'Two' months where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the action must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding paragraphs caution and required form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should include a statement cautioning the patent owner that a complete response should be made since the next action is expected to be an ACP and that requirements of 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should caution that any amendment after an ACP must include 'a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented' to be considered. Insert form paragraph 26.05 (Papers To Be Submitted in Response to Action) and form paragraph 26.73 (Correspondence and Inquiry as to Office Actions) at the end of the Office action. Paragraph 26.05 requires that affidavits/declarations or other documents as evidence of patentability be submitted in response to the Office action; submissions after the next Office action (intended to be an ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d). Paragraph 26.73 provides mailing/fax addresses for correspondence to the CRU.
